correctness.rationale: The six exceptional, fifteen line-transform and six conic-transform classes have pairwise intersection zero or one. Each line has ten neighbors in the double-six presentation; distinct lines through the same point have distinct tangent directions, and Eckardt-freeness excludes triple concurrence, so the 135 intersections give distinct transverse nodes. The connected rational-component divisor has genus 109. The class sum is 27H−9∑E_i=−9K. A separately built double-six graph gives exact Laplacian spectrum 0^1,9^20,15^6 and rooted Smith diagonal 1^7,9^13,45,135^5 at two deletions, with the exact determinant 5129015115539641837921875. The frozen local algorithm correctly clears a minimum-valuation pivot by dividing out its p-power and inverting the unit part; the precision-five runs described by the record resolve all nonzero pivots, and sorting the local valuations aligns the integral invariant factors. Since −K is very ample, the second pencil member can be smooth and avoid the finite node set. In the formal neighborhood of a node the family is given by xy+t·u=0 with u a unit; away from nodes the special fiber is smooth and so is the family there. The pencil is proper and flat over the formal DVR, with smooth geometrically connected generic fiber (Bertini and connectedness for an ample divisor). Thus the regular split thickness-one graph description applies.
residual_risks: Neither Eckardt surfaces nor unequal node thicknesses are covered.

evidence: Theorem 3.1 determines the p-primary group when one nonzero Laplacian eigenvalue is a p-unit; at p=5 the multiplicity of the divisible eigenvalue 15 is six, its valuation is one, and v5(27)=0. This gives (C5)^6. Theorem 3.3 covers valuations one and two at p=3, with r=15, f=6, s=9, g=20, gamma=v3(27)=3. Its two formulas depend on the 3-rank e0.

For the line intersection Gram matrix G, whose diagonal is −1, L=9I−G. The Gram rank over F3 is seven, since the pairing factors through the seven-dimensional Picard lattice and the six E_i together with H−E_1−E_2 form a unimodular basis and hence give an invertible Gram minor modulo three.
broader_coverage.reasoning: With e0=7, the first Theorem 3.3 option asks for f−e0=−1 factors of order three and is impossible, so the second gives f+1−e0=0 factors of order three, g+gamma−2−e0=14 of order nine and e0−gamma+1=5 of order 27. The tree count rules out all other primes. Aligning these with the six order-five factors gives exactly 9^13,45,135^5. No new Smith reduction is needed.

originality.rationale: The exact group is a straightforward specialization of Ducey et al., Critical group structure from the parameters of a strongly regular graph, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3, with a rank forced by the classical line-class marking. That is implication by a relevant prior theorem, not a claim that its Example 3.6 gives the target factors verbatim. The example there is the 16-regular nonintersection graph, whereas both the specialization and the frozen claim concern its 10-regular complement. The divisor and smoothing interpretation use classical geometry and the general component-group theorem.
residual_risks: An earlier written-out table for the target may exist; the conclusion depends on a demonstrated implication, not on locating that table or on assigning same-day priority.

value.rationale: This is a natural degeneration and the exact invariant is potentially useful. But the central numerical result is mechanically implied by earlier strongly regular graph theorems, with the required 3-rank an immediate unimodular-minor fact from the classical double-six marking. The genus, pencil regularity and component-group application here are standard deductions from this same configuration, not a distinct conclusion that sustains the frozen finding on its own.
residual_risks: This assesses the proposed standalone finding, not the utility of compiling known component groups or using the degeneration in another theorem.
